configuration.delivery_shape: paired rows in one source-built static HYLE consumer process
configuration.route: Only pre-v7 public primitives: SpinLock-linearized admission/close, group CancelToken, spawn_task, same-allocator PMR vector of JoinHandle<Status>, per-handle join, first-error aggregation and Scheduler::drain before owner return
configuration.purpose: same-contract migration baseline with the runtime cleanup boundary aligned by a public owner-level fence

ownership_topology.candidate: Each owner creates one allocator-backed TaskScope, admits 32 scope-owned Task<Status> helpers, closes/joins, crosses Scheduler::drain and destroys the scope before returning
ownership_topology.peer: Each owner creates the public group CancelToken, SpinLock close state and same-allocator PMR JoinHandle vector, admits the same helpers with spawn_task, joins all handles, crosses Scheduler::drain and destroys handles/token before returning
ownership_topology.equivalence: Both run in the same direct-source process and use one normal persistent four-worker Scheduler, the same allocator, alternating 4096-owner warmup, common calibrated iteration count, 52 paired interleaved rounds, Task<Status> body, group cancellation, yield, output, failure distribution and owner boundary; Scheduler::drain places every Fiber finish hook, coroutine/driver cleanup and stack return before owner return on both sides

material_contribution.derivation: Inference requests, model loads and rendering frames commonly discover tens of independent helper tasks and must drain them before owner-local resources are released

workloads.semantic_contract: Dynamically discover 32 Status-bearing helper tasks for one owner, stop admission, retain the first business failure, finish all helper runtime cleanup and reclaim owner-local ownership before return

input.distribution: sequential owners; every helper suspends once, one helper fails in roughly one of sixteen owners, and every helper publishes a deterministic output

workloads.setup: Scheduler creation, exact worker placement and alternating 4096 complete warmup owners per route are outside measurement; nanobench compare uses one common iteration count and cyclic Latin-square interleaving for 52 paired rounds of complete owner lifecycles in one direct-source process

one cooperative yield and scheduler reinjection per helper
